new_scholarship.name: International Excellence Entrance Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The University of Manitoba awards one International Excellence Entrance Scholarship valued at $25,000 and two valued at $10,000 each to international high school graduates entering University 1 or any faculty, college or school with a direct entry option. The $25,000 award requires a minimum admission average of 90% across five senior level high school courses, while the two $10,000 awards require only the minimum admission requirements for the programme. Short-listed applicants are ranked first, second and third place using the award application and the admissions application. This is a separate application from the admissions application, although both must be completed.

new_scholarship.name: Killam Predoctoral Scholarship Level 2 (Doctoral)
new_scholarship.official_source: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Graduate Studies
new_scholarship.description: The Faculty of Graduate Studies at Dalhousie University awards Killam Predoctoral Scholarships competitively to outstanding doctoral students across all disciplines, with a base value of $42,000 per year ($14,000 per term) for up to three years. The scholarship is open to both Canadian and international students in a full-time PhD at Dalhousie, and international recipients may only use the funds for study and research in Canada. Applicants who are not eligible to apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D through Dalhousie in the current competition apply through the Faculty of Graduate Studies scholarship platform. The scholarship is supported by the Killam Trusts.

Applicants must demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, strong research potential and a clear likelihood of contributing to the advancement of learning in their field, with character, ethical conduct and contributions to a respectful and inclusive community also considered. The award must be taken up no later than the 7th term of the PhD, and applicants must have spent fewer than six terms (24 months) in the PhD as of May 1 of the award year.

new_scholarship.description: Knight-Hennessy Scholars is a fully-endowed, multidisciplinary leadership development programme for graduate students at Stanford University, with scholars coming from around the globe. During each of the first three years of graduate study scholars receive a fellowship applied directly to cover tuition and associated fees, a stipend for living and academic expenses, and a travel stipend covering an economy-class ticket for one annual trip to and from Stanford. Newly enrolling scholars also receive a one-time relocation stipend, and scholars in their second and third years may apply for supplemental funds for academic enrichment activities. Admission to the funding requires separate but concurrent admission to, and enrolment in, a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme.

new_scholarship.name: Beca al Talento Académico Internacional
new_scholarship.description: The Beca al Talento Académico Internacional is the Tecnológico de Monterrey scholarship for international applicants, reserved for candidates coming from secondary schools in a named group of Latin American and Caribbean countries. It recognises students with an outstanding academic record and can award support of between 40% and 60% of the tuition cost, valid for the campus to which the applicant has been admitted. The call is published once a year for new entrants to the August–December semester, requires a minimum average of 90/100 in bachillerato or high school study, and is limited to candidates under 21 years of age at the time of application. Applicants must be admitted to a professional programme starting in August 2027 and must present the Prueba de Aptitud Académica with a minimum score of 1,360 points, or an equivalent SAT or ACT score converted to that scale.

new_scholarship.description: The Carlos and Clara Quintanilla Scholarship is a $5,000 spring tuition scholarship from the University of Texas at Austin that recognises an undergraduate or graduate student enrolled in the Cockrell School of Engineering. Eligibility is tied to having resided in Mexico immediately before enrolling at the Cockrell School, to good academic standing with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and to demonstrable financial need, and recipients must intend to return to Mexico after graduation.
